items.stem: Due to type erasure in Java generics, which statement is true at runtime?

options.text: Generic type parameters are not available at runtime
options.rationale: Correct: generics are erased, so List<String> and List<Integer> are the same raw type at runtime.

options.text: Each parameterised type creates a distinct runtime class
options.rationale: Erasure means no distinct runtime classes are generated per type argument.

options.text: You can use instanceof List<String> directly
options.rationale: The parameter is erased, so that check is not allowed.

options.text: Primitives can be used directly as type parameters
options.rationale: Type parameters require reference types, hence boxing.

items.explanation: Correct: generics are erased, so parameterised types share one raw type at runtime.

items.stem: What happens if you call a terminal operation on a stream that was already consumed?

options.rationale: Correct: a stream can be operated on only once; reusing it throws IllegalStateException.
Streams do not auto-reset for reuse.

options.text: It returns the previous result from cache
options.rationale: There is no cached-result reuse for a consumed stream.

options.text: It converts the stream into a List
options.rationale: Reuse does not convert the stream; it fails.

items.explanation: Correct: a stream can be operated on only once; reusing it throws IllegalStateException.

items.stem: Which TWO practices help write correct concurrent Java code? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use concurrent collections for shared mutable state
options.rationale: Correct: concurrent collections handle thread-safe access correctly.

options.text: Guard compound check-then-act logic with proper synchronisation
options.rationale: Correct: compound actions are not atomic and need synchronisation.

options.text: Assume all field reads are visible across threads without synchronisation
options.rationale: Without synchronisation/volatile, writes may not be visible to other threads.

options.text: Share a non-thread-safe HashMap across threads freely
options.rationale: A plain HashMap is not thread-safe and can corrupt under concurrent writes.

items.explanation: Correct: concurrent collections and proper synchronisation of compound actions keep concurrent code correct.
